skill.name: documentation
skill.description: Helps teams create, update, and organize Markdown project documentation with templates, rules, and section-level helper scripts.
skill.summary: Standardizes Markdown documentation with templates, workflows, and focused editing helpers.
skill.author: DaoThiHuong2111

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, Mermaid examples, relative documentation links, and example session paths. The main real risk is that bundled Bash helpers can modify caller-supplied files without restricting writes to the documentation tree.

remediation.issue: Write-capable helper scripts accept unrestricted file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate target paths before writing. Prefer allowing only docs/ paths, and reject absolute paths or parent-directory traversal for write operations.

remediation.issue: The skill exposes Bash helpers for documentation maintenance.
remediation.suggestion: Document that script execution should require user confirmation, especially for update, insert, and delete operations.

remediation.issue: Examples and templates trigger many scanner alerts because they contain code fences and relative links.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly marked as Markdown literals and avoid unnecessary shell-looking examples in templates when plain text is enough.

content.value_statement: Project documentation often becomes duplicated, oversized, or hard to navigate. This skill provides templates, rules, and workflows for consistent Markdown documentation.
actual_capabilities: Provides Markdown templates for screen, guide, and architecture documentation.
Defines documentation rules for structure, size limits, examples, and code references.
Includes workflows for creating, updating, splitting, reviewing, and consolidating docs.
Offers Bash helpers for searching, listing, extracting, inserting, updating, and deleting sections.
Encourages screen-based organization and duplicate prevention before new files are created.
limitations: Designed for Markdown documentation in a docs-style project tree.
Bash helper scripts require a Unix-like shell environment.
The skill guides documentation quality but does not verify every code reference automatically.
Write-capable scripts depend on correct file paths and should be used with review.

use_cases.title: Create Screen Documentation
use_cases.description: Use the screen templates to document overview, features, technical details, and user flows for a new screen.

use_cases.title: Update Existing Docs
use_cases.description: Find the right section, read only the relevant content, and update it after code changes.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Documentation Sprawl
use_cases.description: Identify duplicate sections, consolidate overlapping files, and keep documents under the recommended line limit.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Doc
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new documentation page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Markdown documentation for this completed feature. Use the correct template and ask me where it belongs if the location is unclear.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused edit to existing project documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the existing documentation for this behavior and update only the relevant section. Avoid creating a duplicate file.

prompt_templates.title: Review Documentation Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these documentation files for duplicate content, missing examples, oversized files, broken structure, and unclear code references.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate and Restructure Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup across multiple documentation files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this documentation area, propose a consolidation plan, move overlapping content into the right files, and preserve valid links.

output_examples.input: Create docs for a new Home screen.
output_examples.output: A screen documentation set with an overview, feature list, technical notes, flow descriptions, and related file references.

output_examples.input: Update the configuration guide after a setting changed.
output_examples.output: A targeted update to the existing guide section, with the old behavior replaced and examples refreshed.

output_examples.input: Find duplicate documentation about slash commands.
output: A list of likely duplicate sections.
A recommended primary file for the consolidated content.
A checklist for updating links after cleanup.

best_practices: Search for existing documentation before creating a new file.
Keep each document focused and below the recommended line limit.
Use templates and include concrete examples with traceable file references.
anti_patterns: Creating a new document when an existing section should be updated.
Mixing user guides, architecture notes, and screen details in one large file.
Running write-capable helper scripts without checking the target path first.

faq.question: What type of documentation does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Markdown project documentation, especially screen docs, architecture notes, developer guides, and workflow references.

faq.question: Does it create documentation from code automatically?
faq.answer: It can help draft documentation from provided context, but it relies on the agent to inspect relevant code and user requirements.

faq.question: Can it update existing documentation instead of creating duplicates?
faq.answer: Yes. Its workflows prioritize search, section extraction, and targeted updates before new files are created.

faq.question: Are the bundled scripts required?
faq.answer: No. They are optional helpers for section-level work, but the templates and rules can be used manually.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users review before running scripts?
faq.answer: Users should confirm the file path, section name, and content file because some scripts can modify Markdown files.
